final_decision.reason: KEEP exp-003 as the final frozen configuration because it is the numeric validation winner: reducing max_depth from 4 to 3 raised validation AUPRC from 0.48299 to 0.48672 (+0.00373) and validation AUROC from 0.88640 to 0.88693. The gain is smaller than the aspirational 0.490 target, but it is positive under the official selection metric and no further experiments remain in budget.
final_decision.learning: Shallower trees modestly improved ranking while materially reducing the train-validation AUPRC gap from 0.24394 (0.72692 vs 0.48299) to 0.17285 (0.65957 vs 0.48672). At the selected best-F1 threshold, false negatives fell from 235 to 208 and recall rose from 0.45093 to 0.51402, including Q4-high ERC recall from 0.55249 to 0.59669 and VIIRS-match recall from 0.90722 to 0.92784; however false positives rose from 211 to 299 and Brier score worsened from 0.09702 to 0.10325. Thus depth 3 is the best validation ranking configuration, with a threshold-dependent precision/calibration tradeoff that does not overturn the AUPRC selection criterion.
final_decision.next_question: After freezing exp-003 without further tuning, what AUPRC does it achieve on the sealed official 2020 test year, and how does that one-time result compare with the published 0.533 test benchmark?

history.hypothesis: Establish the metadata-only logistic regression baseline (fixed setup, not chosen by ARIA).
history.decision_reason: Keep exp-000 as the valid metadata-only reference: it completed on the official 2019 validation split and provides the baseline AUPRC and error profile needed to measure subsequent gains, although it is not yet a competitive final candidate.
history.decision_learning: Metadata-only logistic regression has limited validation ranking performance (AUPRC 0.1842), a substantial train-to-validation AUPRC gap of 0.1434, and errors concentrated in high-fire-danger and VIIRS-matched positives; its strongest coefficients being geographic indicators suggests reliance on location-specific associations.
history.next_question: Does adding all allowed discovery-time environmental and remote-sensing features, without changing the model or regularization, lift validation AUPRC above 0.220 and reduce misses in high-ERC and VIIRS-matched positives?

history.hypothesis: Keeping logistic regression and its hyperparameters fixed while changing only the feature protocol from metadata to all will raise validation AUPRC above 0.220 by adding weather/fire-danger, VIIRS, fuel, vegetation, topography, access, and population signals that are available at discovery time.
history.observation: The metadata-only logistic baseline reached validation AUPRC 0.1842 versus train AUPRC 0.3276 and missed 269 of 428 validation positives. Its largest standardized coefficients are mostly county/state indicators, while it missed 119 of 181 positives in the Q4-high ERC group and 68 of 97 positives with a VIIRS match, indicating that metadata alone is not capturing measured fire-danger and active-fire signals.
history.expected_result: Validation AUPRC of at least 0.220 (an absolute gain of at least 0.036 over 0.1842), with fewer than 119 false negatives among Q4-high ERC positives and fewer than 68 false negatives among VIIRS-matched positives at the reported best-F1 threshold.
history.reason: This isolates one meaningful variable—the feature protocol—while preserving model, C, class weighting, and weather_days. The measured concentration of false negatives in high-ERC and VIIRS-matched cases makes the official full input the most direct test of whether omitted discovery-time environmental and remote-sensing features explain the baseline's weak ranking performance.
history.decision_reason: Exp-001 decisively improved validation AUPRC to 0.3972 from 0.1842 (+0.2130) and exceeded its >=0.220 target. It also met both error-profile expectations, reducing Q4-high ERC false negatives below 119 to 99 and VIIRS-match false negatives below 68 to 19, while cutting overall false positives from 638 to 240.
history.decision_learning: The official full discovery-time feature set adds strong ranking signal beyond metadata, especially for VIIRS-matched fires, but full-feature logistic regression still has a large train-validation AUPRC gap (0.7213 vs 0.3972) and misses 262 of 428 validation positives, indicating that model form or regularization is now the main question rather than feature availability.
history.next_question: Can a nonlinear tree ensemble with early stopping exploit the validated full-input signal better than the linear model and raise validation AUPRC to at least 0.430 without changing the feature protocol or weather window?

history.hypothesis: Keeping the full feature protocol and five weather days fixed while replacing logistic regression with the official bounded XGBoost configuration will capture nonlinear interactions among weather, VIIRS, fuel, vegetation, and location and raise validation AUPRC to at least 0.430.
history.observation: Exp-001 raised validation AUPRC from 0.1842 to 0.3972 (+0.2130) by changing only metadata to the full feature protocol. It also reduced false positives from 638 to 240, VIIRS-match false negatives from 68/97 positives to 19/97, and Q4-high ERC false negatives from 119/181 to 99/181. However, train AUPRC is 0.7213 versus validation AUPRC 0.3972, and the linear model still misses 262/428 validation positives; several of its largest coefficients are individual county or categorical vegetation/fuel indicators.
history.expected_result: Validation AUPRC >= 0.430, an absolute improvement of at least 0.0328 over exp-001; otherwise the hypothesis is rejected and exp-001 remains the preferred configuration.
history.reason: This tests one meaningful variable: model family. The feature protocol, weather window, data split, and metric remain fixed. Exp-001 proves the full discovery-time features carry substantial signal, while its 0.3241 train-validation AUPRC gap and prominent categorical coefficients motivate a tree ensemble with early stopping and bounded official defaults to model interactions without changing the inputs.
history.decision_reason: Exp-002 exceeded its validation target of 0.430, raising validation AUPRC to 0.4830 from 0.3972 (+0.0858). It also improved validation AUROC from 0.8384 to 0.8864, reduced false negatives from 262 to 235 and false positives from 240 to 211, and improved both Q4-high ERC and VIIRS-match recall.
history.decision_learning: The nonlinear XGBoost model extracts materially more validation ranking signal from the same full discovery-time inputs than logistic regression. However, train AUPRC 0.7269 versus validation AUPRC 0.4830 leaves a 0.2439 gap, so reducing tree complexity is the highest-value remaining single-variable test.
history.next_question: Can reducing max_depth from 4 to 3 preserve the validated nonlinear signal while narrowing overfitting enough to raise validation AUPRC above 0.4830?

payload.reason: KEEP exp-003 as the final frozen configuration because it is the numeric validation winner: reducing max_depth from 4 to 3 raised validation AUPRC from 0.48299 to 0.48672 (+0.00373) and validation AUROC from 0.88640 to 0.88693. The gain is smaller than the aspirational 0.490 target, but it is positive under the official selection metric and no further experiments remain in budget.
payload.learning: Shallower trees modestly improved ranking while materially reducing the train-validation AUPRC gap from 0.24394 (0.72692 vs 0.48299) to 0.17285 (0.65957 vs 0.48672). At the selected best-F1 threshold, false negatives fell from 235 to 208 and recall rose from 0.45093 to 0.51402, including Q4-high ERC recall from 0.55249 to 0.59669 and VIIRS-match recall from 0.90722 to 0.92784; however false positives rose from 211 to 299 and Brier score worsened from 0.09702 to 0.10325. Thus depth 3 is the best validation ranking configuration, with a threshold-dependent precision/calibration tradeoff that does not overturn the AUPRC selection criterion.
payload.next_question: After freezing exp-003 without further tuning, what AUPRC does it achieve on the sealed official 2020 test year, and how does that one-time result compare with the published 0.533 test benchmark?
